reason: Conversation 2 gathers the key facts (one zone, front/high, flashing code, drawer timing, loud fan) and correctly reasons that a roaring fan indicates the fan is working and that restricted ventilation from the new drawer is the most likely cause, then gives the right escalation: ask the kitchen installer to check clearances against the hob's installation instructions, with an engineer only if clearances are correct. Conversation 1 reaches the broadly right direction (overheat protection, ventilation gap) but when told about the new drawer it says 'Nothing changes' and jumps straight to an engineer, failing to connect the drawer to the fault or suggest the installer re-check clearance, and never asks about the code or zone. Both avoid unsupported part recommendations and stay within the safety boundary; neither mandates the homeowner go under the hob after they refused.
